definitions.explanation: A piece of furniture for sitting, typically with a back and four legs. Can refer to any type of chair.

examples.japanese: {椅子|いす}に{座|すわ}ってください。
この{椅子|いす}は{高|たか}いですね。
examples.english: This chair is tall, isn't it?

examples.japanese: {会議室|かいぎしつ}に{椅子|いす}が{足|た}りないので、{隣|となり}の{部屋|へや}から{持|も}ってきてください。
examples.english: There aren't enough chairs in the meeting room, so please bring some from the next room.

examples.japanese: この{椅子|いす}は{長|なが}い{時間|じかん}{座|すわ}っても{疲|つか}れないので、{仕事|しごと}をするときにとても{便利|べんり}です。
examples.english: This chair doesn't make you tired even if you sit for a long time, so it's very convenient for working.

notes:
{椅子|いす} is the general word for chair, often written in hiragana as いす.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {椅子|いす}に{座|すわ}る: to sit on a chair
- {椅子|いす}から{立|た}つ: to stand up from a chair
- {椅子|いす}を{引|ひ}く: to pull out a chair
- {椅子|いす}を{並|なら}べる: to line up chairs

COUNTER:
{脚|きゃく} for chairs (because they have legs). Also つ or {個|こ} in casual speech.

TYPES OF SEATING:
- ソファー: sofa
- ベンチ: bench
- {回転|かいてん}{椅子|いす}: swivel chair
- {折|お}りたたみ{椅子|いす}: folding chair

Note: For traditional Japanese floor seating, see {座布団|ざぶとん} (floor cushion).
